capabilities: Export vault settings, hotkeys, workspace, and plugin manifests to a single .nix file
Import a .nix file and write config and plugin settings back to .obsidian/
Toggle which config files (app, appearance, core plugins, graph, workspace, hotkeys, plugin data) are included
Generate an obsidian-activate.sh script that evaluates the .nix file with nix and applies it for NixOS or home-manager
Strip machine-specific workspace fields such as last-open files and active panel state
disambiguation: Not a vault-content sync tool; it only round-trips settings and plugin configs as Nix data, not notes or plugin JS files.
extras: Import accepts only literal Nix values; hand-edited files with interpolation, function calls, or let/in will fail or corrupt values. Plugin JS files are not exported, so Obsidian still downloads plugins itself. Plugin data.json may contain secrets, so plugin-settings export can be disabled. The plugin has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian stores config in .obsidian/ JSON files that are hard to version-control or apply declaratively on machines managed with Nix.

relations.evidence: The script takes the exported .nix file, evaluates it with nix eval --json
Generate NixOS integration files | off | Also exports obsidian-activate.sh

summary: Exports Obsidian vault settings and plugin configs to a .nix file and imports them back, with an optional NixOS/home-manager activation script.
